stem: A 35-year-old woman presents with fatigue, pallor, and brittle nails. Laboratory tests reveal microcytic hypochromic anemia. Which laboratory pattern is most consistent with the underlying cause of her anemia?

keywords: Microcytic hypochromic anemia – Indicates iron deficiency anemia or other microcytic causes; helps narrow lab pattern.
Brittle nails – Classic physical sign of iron deficiency (koilonychia).
Fatigue & pallor – Non-specific but supports anemia; part of the classic triad of iron deficiency anemia (Fatigue + Pallor + Koilonychia).
keywordsHtml:
1. Microcytic hypochromic anemia – Indicates iron deficiency anemia or other microcytic causes; helps narrow lab pattern.
  2. Brittle nails – Classic physical sign of iron deficiency (koilonychia).
  3. Fatigue & pallor – Non-specific but supports anemia; part of the classic triad of iron deficiency anemia (Fatigue + Pallor + Koilonychia).

A.title: Low serum iron, high TIBC, low ferritin
A.body:
Why correct: This pattern is classic for iron deficiency anemia.
Low serum iron → reduced circulating iron due to depletion.
High TIBC → liver produces more transferrin to scavenge iron.
Low ferritin → reflects depleted iron stores.
Patients typically present with fatigue, pallor, brittle nails, and sometimes pica.
A.bodyHtml:
• Why correct: This pattern is classic for iron deficiency anemia.
    • Low serum iron → reduced circulating iron due to depletion.
    • High TIBC → liver produces more transferrin to scavenge iron.
    • Low ferritin → reflects depleted iron stores.
  • Patients typically present with fatigue, pallor, brittle nails, and sometimes pica.

B.title: Low serum iron, low TIBC, high ferritin
B.body:
Seen in anemia of chronic disease (ACD).
Iron is sequestered in storage; transferrin production is low → low TIBC.
Ferritin is normal or high (an acute-phase reactant), unlike iron deficiency.
B.bodyHtml:
• Seen in anemia of chronic disease (ACD).
  • Iron is sequestered in storage; transferrin production is low → low TIBC.
  • Ferritin is normal or high (an acute-phase reactant), unlike iron deficiency.

C.title: High serum iron, high ferritin, low TIBC
C.body:
Seen in iron overload states (e.g., hemochromatosis).
Not consistent with microcytic anemia; usually leads to organ deposition.
C.bodyHtml:
• Seen in iron overload states (e.g., hemochromatosis).
  • Not consistent with microcytic anemia; usually leads to organ deposition.

D.title: Low serum iron, normal TIBC, normal ferritin
D.body:
Could indicate early or mild iron deficiency, but classic lab pattern is high TIBC and low ferritin.
Less likely as the “most consistent” pattern for iron deficiency anemia.
D.bodyHtml:
• Could indicate early or mild iron deficiency, but classic lab pattern is high TIBC and low ferritin.
  • Less likely as the “most consistent” pattern for iron deficiency anemia.

E.title: High serum iron, low TIBC, high ferritin
E.body: Seen in sideroblastic anemia or hemolytic anemia with iron release, not typical iron deficiency.
E.bodyHtml: • Seen in sideroblastic anemia or hemolytic anemia with iron release, not typical iron deficiency.

keyConcept:
Iron deficiency anemia is a microcytic hypochromic anemia characterized by low serum iron, high TIBC, and low ferritin, reflecting depleted iron stores and compensatory increase in transferrin.
Clinical presentation includes fatigue, pallor, brittle nails, spoon nails, and sometimes pica.
keyConceptHtml:
• Iron deficiency anemia is a microcytic hypochromic anemia characterized by low serum iron, high TIBC, and low ferritin, reflecting depleted iron stores and compensatory increase in transferrin.
  • Clinical presentation includes fatigue, pallor, brittle nails, spoon nails, and sometimes pica.
classicTriad: Fatigue + Pallor + Brittle nails (Koilonychia) → suggests iron deficiency anemia, guiding the choice of low serum iron, high TIBC, low ferritin.

diagram.name: Laboratory Diagnosis
diagram.caption: This diagram illustrates the characteristic laboratory findings of iron deficiency anemia, including low serum iron, high TIBC, and low ferritin, along with peripheral smear features showing microcytic, hypochromic red blood cells. It also correlates these findings with common clinical features such as fatigue, pallor, and brittle nails, helping in quick visual diagnosis and exam recall.
